newsitem.title: USA: Ethanol blends with tobacco in U.S. Senate debate.
newsitem.headline: Ethanol blends with tobacco in U.S. Senate debate.

text.p: Senator Jesse Helms turned the tables on antismoking activists in the U.S. Senate on Wednesday, proposing higher fuel taxes on ethanol to help pay for federal antismoking programs.

Helms proposed a three-cent a gallon increase in ethanol taxes, which would halve the ethanol tax break, now worth 5.4 cents a gallon at the pump. Revenue from the tax would go to a newly created trust fund to be available to the Health and Human Services Department for antismoking programs.
Two Midwestern Democrats, Dick Durbin of Illinois and Tom Harkin of Iowa, offered anti-tobacco amendments earlier in the day during debate on fiscal 1998 agriculture appropriations.
The Harkin amendment would put a 1.1 percent assessment on tobacco company purchases of raw tobacco with the funds to be used to pay for ID checks of youthful smokers.
Durbin proposed a ban on federally subsidized crop insurance for tobacco growers.
The marketing assessment involved in Harkin amendment has existed at a lesser rate since 1990, and is unrelated to the tobacco tax in the U.S. budget bill.
